fixes.find: The CIA turned the money down, while running its own operations against Allende; two ITT officials were later charged with lying to the Senate about it.
fixes.replace: The offer was turned down, while the CIA ran its own operations against Allende. In 1978 two ITT officials were charged with lying to the Senate about the company's actions in Chile; in 1979 the government dropped the case against one of them, Robert Berrellez, saying a trial would expose national security information.
fixes.why: The $1 million was offered through John McCone to CIA director Helms and to Kissinger, and Kissinger wrote that he turned it down (EBSCO), so 'the CIA' alone is too narrow. Charges against Edward Gerrity and Robert Berrellez in 1978 confirmed (Harvard Crimson 1978); the Berrellez case was dropped on national security grounds (News Journal, 9 Feb 1979). How the Gerrity case ended could not be confirmed, so it is left unstated. https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/history/itt-actions-cause-suspicion-involvement-chilean-coup ; https://www.thecrimson.com/article/1978/4/5/the-discreet-lies-of-itt-pii/ ; https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/161291565/
